blocks.text:
# Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6.     # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run

    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →

2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same

blocks.text:
# Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi

The agent loop then sees an empty stream → `result` completes with StateError('EventStream ended without a completion event')... actually `end()` without result → result completes with StateError. Actually, let me check what AssistantMessageEventStream.push does when the controller is closed — `stream.end()` sets `_done=true`; pushes after end are ignored (`if (_done) return`). So push-after-end never throws! The only throw sources: `_events()` construction (cast errors), `stream.push` before end (controller not closed — `_controller.add` on a paused... single-subscription controller buffers; never throws), and `stream.end()` itself (doesn't throw). And `Future.delayed` never throws. So the `on Object` catch ONLY ever fires for script-construction errors (cast errors) — the stated rationale ("consumer gone") is wrong, and it converts a loud script bug into a silently-empty turn. That makes the finding slightly stronger: misleading comment + swallowed errors. Still SUGGESTION (test-only tooling) but a legit one.

2. **Duplication in `_events`**: the thinking and text blocks are near-identical (~30 lines each). jscpd gate: core lib/ < 1%. Would this trip jscpd? The blocks are within a single function in one file; jscpd counts clones across files typically (configured in crap4dart.yaml / jscpd config). Let me check the jscpd config quickly. If a throw occurs between BSU and try-entry... nothing between them except var declaration. The only throw risk is the BSU write itself (broken pipe) — then no ESU, but the process is dying anyway. Negligible.

5. **CellRenderer catch block: `on Object { _syncEnd(); rethrow; }`** — if `_syncEnd()` itself throws (write to broken sink), that exception replaces the original. Negligible edge.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also

# Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi

The agent loop then sees an empty stream → `result` completes with StateError('EventStream ended without a completion event')... actually `end()` without result → result completes with StateError. Actually, let me check what AssistantMessageEventStream.push does when the controller is closed — `stream.end()` sets `_done=true`; pushes after end are ignored (`if (_done) return`). So push-after-end never throws! The only throw sources: `_events()` construction (cast errors), `stream.push` before end (controller not closed — `_controller.add` on a paused... single-subscription controller buffers; never throws), and `stream.end()` itself (doesn't throw). And `Future.delayed` never throws. So the `on Object` catch ONLY ever fires for script-construction errors (cast errors) — the stated rationale ("consumer gone") is wrong, and it converts a loud script bug into a silently-empty turn. ## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;
  child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly (issue #553).
  Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps the full
  real-provider suite (pty-integration).
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the

- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet

blocks.text:
# Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi

The agent loop then sees an empty stream → `result` completes with StateError('EventStream ended without a completion event')... actually `end()` without result → result completes with StateError. What does the agent loop do with that? Depends. But the loud alternative (letting the cast error propagate as an unhandled async error) would crash the process with a clear stack. Actually, let me check what AssistantMessageEventStream.push does when the controller is closed — `stream.end()` sets `_done=true`; pushes after end are ignored (`if (_done) return`). So push-after-end never throws! The only throw sources: `_events()` construction (cast errors), `stream.push` before end (controller not closed — `_controller.add` on a paused... single-subscription controller buffers; never throws), and `stream.end()` itself (doesn't throw). And `Future.delayed` never throws. So the `on Object` catch ONLY ever fires for script-construction errors (cast errors) — the stated rationale ("consumer gone") is wrong, and it converts a loud script bug into a silently-empty turn. tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test

Now, an important question about the self-heal test: the frames counter increments per `view()` call. The flow: init → 30ms → `_FrameMsg('first')` → update sets throwNext=false, returns cmd for 30ms → `_FrameMsg('poison')` → update sets throwNext=true → 30ms → view() throws (frame 2? Actually view is called during render: first frame renders 'frame-ok-1', then msg 'first' → needsRender → view renders 'frame-ok-2', then 'poison' msg → view renders frame 3 which throws. Guard catches, invalidates, enqueues RenderTickMsg. RenderTick → applyMsg returns true → renderGuarded → view() frame 4 → 'frame-ok-4' → healed... wait 'poison' → next is 'healed', then 'quit'.

Wait, actually the test comment says "Each frame is its OWN batch: a 30ms-spaced cmd chain keeps every frame outside the 16ms fps-throttle window". The render of 'frame-ok-2' happens after the 'first' message. Then 'poison' message arrives 30ms later → render → view() throws. Test expects `frames >= 3` and output contains 'frame-ok-' but not 'poison'. OK.

The assertions: `expect(sink.buf.toString(), isNot(contains('poison')))` — the label 'poison' is only in the msg, never in view content, so this assertion trivially passes even if the poisoned frame rendered nothing. Hmm, `view()` throws BEFORE returning the View, so 'poison' never paints. But if the guard were broken (render threw and killed the pipeline), the test would hang past the 5s timeout because QuitMsg would never process... actually would it? If render throws inside the loop and propagates, `_runCore` finally runs and the program exits with error — run() would complete with a thrown error? The exception would propagate out of `run` → test fails with error. And `frames >= 3` confirms subsequent frames painted after the throw. And `contains('frame-ok-')` confirms painting. Reasonable test.

One thing: `isNot(contains('poison'))` — since 'poison' never appears in any view content (labels are 'first'/'poison'/'healed'/'quit' — wait, view content is 'frame-ok-$frames'). The 'poison' string only appears in the msg label, never in view output. So this assertion passes trivially regardless. It's a guard against a hypothetical where the poison label leaks into output. Weak but harmless.

Now the self-heal test asserts "the next frame DID paint — and, because the guard invalidated the renderer, it is a FULL repaint (first-frame clear)". But the test only checks `contains('frame-ok-')` — it does NOT actually verify the full repaint happened (e.g., checking for the first-frame clear sequence `\x1b[K` per row or ESU boundaries). The comment claims more than the assertion verifies. SUGGESTION: strengthen assertion or soften comment.

Now, check the program.dart guard again for a potential issue:

```dart
} catch (e, st) {
  if (!renderedOnce) rethrow;
  ...

}
```

`enqueue` — let me check what enqueue does vs send. Also, RenderTickMsg handling in applyMsg returns true, which triggers `renderGuarded(force: false)`... wait, in the loop: `needsRender |= await applyMsg(msg)` and then `if (needsRender && _running) await renderGuarded(force: inputDriven)`. RenderTick is not a KeyMsg so inputDriven=false. The guard sets `lastRenderMicros = -1` so the fps throttle passes. Good.

But consider: render fails → guard sets redrawArmed=false, enqueues RenderTick → loop drains → applyMsg(RenderTickMsg) returns true → renderGuarded → if view throws again (permanently throwing view): renderedOnce=true, lastRenderFailed was set true → repeatFailure=true → no re-enqueue. So it stops hot-spinning. Then the loop continues with waitForActivity. When a REAL message arrives, applyMsg → needsRender → renderGuarded → throws → repeatFailure is... wait: lastRenderFailed is true from previous failure, so repeatFailure = true → no re-enqueue. Hmm, then when does it retry after healing? If the view heals (stops throwing), the next real message renders fine. But if the view throws on EVERY render attempt, after the second failure it never re-enqueues ticks, so failures are logged only on real messages. That matches the comment: "A repeat retry lands only on the next REAL message". Actually the retry IS the real message's render. OK, design is coherent.

One subtle issue: after a failure, `lastRenderMicros = -1` — but the fps throttle check is `lastRenderMicros >= 0 && minFrameMicros > 0 && !force` → -1 skips the throttle. Fine, deliberate.

Another subtlety: `redrawArmed = false` — if a redraw timer was pending (Timer with `redrawArmed = false` inside its callback)... setting redrawArmed=false while a Timer is still pending: when the timer fires, it sets `redrawArmed = false` again and enqueues a RenderTick if `_running`. Wait, actually there's a potential concern: the timer callback enqueues RenderTick → applyMsg returns true → render → succeeds → `redrawArmed` already false. fine.

Now — `renderedOnce` vs. the fps-drop path: render() can return early WITHOUT painting when a frame is dropped (delta < minFrameMicros). In that case `renderedOnce = true` is still set... wait:

await render(_runningModel!.view, force: force);
renderedOnce = true;

But the initial first-frame render is `force: true`, so it can't drop. And by definition a dropped frame means a previous frame painted within the window... not necessarily: `lastRenderMicros = -1` initial → first non-forced render can't drop either (lastRenderMicros >= 0 fails). And the guard sets lastRenderMicros = -1 on failure. So `renderedOnce = true` after a dropped frame implies an earlier successful paint. OK, sound.

Edge: `_renderer?.invalidate()` on failure — but if `_renderer` is null (disabled renderer)? Then nothing to invalidate; NilRenderer. fine.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;
  child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly (issue #553).
  Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps the full
  real-provider suite (pty-integration).
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet
  CHANGED lines via `scripts/diff_coverage.py`); jscpd duplication < 1%
  core `lib/`, < 3.7% `flutter_app/lib/` (ratchet — only tighten).
- Cross-module duplication (issue #487): clones spanning module roots
  (`lib`, `bin`, `flutter_app/lib`, `packages/*/lib`, `browser_ext/dart`)

# Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed

blocks.text:
# Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since

# Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in

# Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi

arguments.content:
# AC3 self-heal test is not executed by any CI leg

⚠️ **IMPORTANT**

This new test is the only proof of gh-1197 AC3 (a throwing `view()` self-heals instead of freezing the pipeline), but nothing in CI or the pre-commit gate runs `vendor/dart_tui`'s own test suite — no workflow or `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` step ever invokes `dart test` inside `vendor/dart_tui` (the only CI reference to the vendor fork is the publish-resolution check in `ci.yml`). The changes it covers (`program.dart` `renderGuarded`, `renderer.dart` sync-close guards) therefore have **zero automated gating**: a future vendor resync or refactor could silently re-break AC3 and every CI leg would stay green.

Options:
- Add a gate/CI stage running `dart test` in `vendor/dart_tui` (fast, hermetic), or
- Port this scenario into the root package's suite (e.g. alongside the other dart_tui-facing tests) so the existing shards pick it up.

# `_play`'s catch-all can only fire for script-construction errors — and swallows them

💡 **SUGGESTION**

The comment says this catch exists for a gone consumer, but `stream.push()` after `end()` is a no-op (`EventStream.push` guards on `_done`) and `Future.delayed` never throws — so in practice the only exceptions that can reach this `on Object` are cast errors from `_events()` (e.g. a malformed `tool_call` step missing `id`). The effect: a typo'd test script becomes a **silently empty turn** (the stream ends with zero events and the agent loop gets `StateError('EventStream ended without a completion event')`) instead of a loud crash pointing at the bad step.

Consider materializing the event list before the `try`, or rethrowing with the script step's context, so script bugs fail fast and loudly.

# Duplicated paced-block emit loops (thinking vs text)

💡 **SUGGESTION**

The `thinking` block below and the `text` block after it are ~25 lines of near-identical logic (append to `blocks`, start event, paced delta loop with `partial(content: List.of(blocks))`, end event, `contentIndex++`). Only the event constructors and content-block type differ. Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in

4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;
  child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly (issue #553).

# Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.
    # Merge-blocking through the EXISTING legs: ci.yml test-core (dart test
    # runs it) and the pty-visual job (fa_omp_reg_visual_test.dart) both
    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new
    # stage. Standalone: dart test test/cli/omp_reg_parity_test.dart

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;
  child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly (issue #553).
  Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps the full
  real-provider suite (pty-integration).
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet
  CHANGED lines via `scripts/diff_coverage.py`); jscpd duplication < 1%
  core `lib/`, < 3.7% `flutter_app/lib/` (ratchet — only tighten).
- Cross-module duplication (issue #487): clones spanning module roots

# Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;
  child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly (issue #553).
  Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps the full
  real-provider suite (pty-integration).
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the

- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet

# Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi

{"content":"# `_play`'s catch-all can only fire for script-construction errors — and swallows them

💡 **SUGGESTION**

The comment says this catch exists for a gone consumer, but `stream.push()` after `end()` is a no-op (`EventStream.push` guards on `_done`) and `Future.delayed` never throws — so in practice the only exceptions that can reach this `on Object` are cast errors from `_events()` (e.g. a malformed `tool_call` step missing `id`). The effect: a typo'd test script becomes a **silently empty turn** (the stream ends with zero events and the agent loop gets `StateError('EventStream ended without a completion event')`) instead of a loud crash pointing at the bad step.

Consider materializing the event list before the `try`, or rethrowing with the script step's context, so script bugs fail fast and loudly.
